caption_or_description: Refraction through glass. Although dashed line AC is the shortest path, light takes a slightly longer path through the air from A to a, then a shorter path through the glass to c, and then to C. The emerging light is displaced but parallel to the incident light.
Because of atmospheric refraction, when the Sun is near the horizon, it appears to be higher in the sky.
Check Your Answer diagram showing the seal’s path of least time bending differently because it can swim faster than it can run.
Refraction relates to indices of refraction in accord with Snell’s law.

Light from the sky picks up speed in the air near the ground because that air is hotter and less dense than the air above. When the light grazes the surface and bends upward, the observer sees a mirage.
The Sun’s shape is distorted by differential refraction.
